{"type":"text","text":"# Work unit U-0002

Rules: use_concepts_for_templates

## Files in the unit

### include/meta/format.h

```cpp
#ifndef META_FORM

edits.search:
template <typename T>
typename std::enable_if<is_container<T>::value, std::string>::type toString(const T& value) {
edits.replace:
template <typename T>
std::string toString(const T& value) requires is_container<T>::value {

arguments.summary: The remaining enable_if constraints become requires-clauses: the pair and container overloads of toString, and Quantity's specialization for arithmetic types.
review_notes: meta::enable_if_c in traits.h still wraps std::enable_if: it is a public helper that nothing in the project uses any more, and removing it would change the public API, which this rule keeps. It can go in an API-changing cleanup.
Quantity's primary template keeps its Enable parameter, so Quantity<T> and Quantity<T, void> name the same types as before.
